podcast-dannyjones-QjmzctByDx0:
Chase Hughes teaches behavior profiling and persuasion, drawing on military and intelligence training, and he joins Danny Jones to open the mind of a master manipulator. Hughes explains the levers of influence he says professionals use: authority, rapport, and the quiet steering of attention and emotion.

The episode doubles as a defense manual; Hughes argues that knowing the techniques is the only real protection against them. Jones asks for demonstrations and war stories, and Hughes obliges within the limits of a public conversation. His credentials and claims are his own presentation, and listeners can test the methods against their own experience of being persuaded, which is the homework he assigns. Few episodes in the series hand the audience a usable skill. This one aims to.
podcast-dannyjones-yGiEwVos3x0:
Author John Perkins joins Danny Jones to talk about the shadow government, the World Bank, and CIA-backed coups. Perkins is known for his book Confessions of an Economic Hit Man. He claims he once bent poor lands for US firms.

Perkins tells how loans were used as a trap to own a land's wealth and votes. He argues the same game still runs, with new tools and the same aims. Jones asks what proof he can show from his own years in the game. Listeners get a famous tale from the man who says he played it. The library holds the talk as an archive record.

Raul Bilecky sits down with Rogan for episode 2449 of the Joe Rogan Experience, a full-length entry in the show's long run of open conversations. The episode keeps the format the show is known for: one guest, hours of talk, no fixed script or segment breaks.

Without a single set topic, the conversation follows the guest's own ground, and the transcript preserves the whole exchange as it aired. Readers can follow the turns a long Rogan talk takes when it is left to wander. The entry serves listeners who want the complete session on file, in the guest's own words from start to finish.
